title: Microsoft Agent 365: registry sync from external AI platforms
summary: Hold: the briefing says Microsoft has not confirmed whether the registry APIs cover synchronised agents, although its cited guide says they retrieve a complete tenant inventory. The documented paths, synchronisation limitations and licensing caveats otherwise match the sources. Several checklist controls also have no corresponding table row.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes discovering agents outside Microsoft and automatically syncing them into the registry.
claims.quote: Connect to external AI platforms to discover agents created outside Microsoft and automatically sync them into the Agent 365 registry for more complete agent visibility and governance.

claims.claim: Coverage depends on the platform and what it exposes, not every agent on that platform necessarily being included.
claims.quote: Coverage depends on the connected platform and the agents it exposes, so a registry entry represents the supported information available from that source - not a guarantee that every agent on the platform is included.

claims.claim: Synced agents enter the same registry inventory as Microsoft and in-house agents.
claims.quote: The agent registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center lists the agents in your organization. It includes agents from Microsoft, from partners, and from your own teams.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Connection credentials are stored as encrypted connection data within Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Agent 365 stores the credentials that you enter for a connection as encrypted connection data within Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Every currently supported platform requires a key-based credential.
claims.quote: Every currently supported platform requires a key-based credential, such as an API key, secret, or private key.

claims.claim: Connected platforms does not currently support keyless authentication options such as workload identity federation or role assumption.
claims.quote: Keyless authentication options, such as workload identity federation or role assumption, aren't currently supported for Connected platforms.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Collect agent observability data is enabled by default for new connections.
claims.quote: New connections have this setting enabled by default.

claims.claim: Observability collection retrieves source-platform agent activity telemetry using the stored connection credentials.
claims.quote: When you enable this setting, Microsoft 365 retrieves agent activity telemetry—such as agent sessions, usage, and related operational signals—from the connected platform by using the connection's stored credentials.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Telemetry retrieval can query services such as Google BigQuery or Amazon S3 and incur provider-billed data access or query charges.
claims.quote: Retrieving agent telemetry from the connected platform might query the provider's own logging or data services (for example, Google BigQuery or Amazon S3) and can incur data access or query charges that the provider bills.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Agent 365 does not invoke, execute or interact with source-platform agents through these connections.
claims.quote: Agent 365 never invokes, executes, or interacts with agents in the source platform.

claims.claim: The general connection security model is read-only except for an explicit administrator removal action.
claims.quote: Agent 365 doesn't write to, modify, or delete resources in the source platform. The only exception is an explicit administrator action to remove a synchronized agent

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The general guide describes source-agent removal as requiring a separate optional delete permission that administrators can omit.
claims.quote: The only exception is an explicit administrator action to remove a synchronized agent, which requires a separate, optional delete permission that you can choose not to grant.

claims.claim: The Google Vertex AI guide includes aiplatform.reasoningEngines.delete in the permissions to grant.
claims.quote:
Grant the service account the Vertex AI permissions required for agent discovery and management:

aiplatform.reasoningEngines.list
aiplatform.reasoningEngines.get
aiplatform.reasoningEngines.delete

claims.claim: Databricks Genie activity collection requires Can Manage.
claims.quote: Activity requires Can Manage. Databricks returns the conversations of all users of a Genie agent only to principals that have Can Manage permission.

claims.claim: Databricks Can Manage also permits moving a Genie agent to the trash when an administrator removes it in Agent 365.
claims.quote: The only exception is when an administrator removes a synchronized agent in Agent 365 and the service principal has Can Manage permission on the Genie agent. In that case, Agent 365 moves the Genie agent to the trash in Databricks.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Agent 365 uses a fixed set of outbound IP addresses that restricted source platforms must allow.
claims.quote: Agent 365 calls source platform APIs from a fixed set of outbound IP addresses. If your organization restricts network access to a source platform, allow traffic from these addresses before you create the connection.

claims.claim: Source-platform network restrictions can produce an authentication failure even with correct credentials.
claims.quote: When a network restriction blocks Agent 365, the connection can fail with the message Authentication failed. Please check your credentials and try again., even when the credentials are correct.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents Graph APIs for listing agents in the tenant inventory.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not say whether the documented registry inventory APIs cover synchronised agents.
claims.quote: Get all agents in your inventory: Use the List packages API, to retrieve a complete list of agents in your tenant for compliance and reporting.
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence with: "The Graph agent registry APIs Microsoft documents list agents in the tenant inventory; those references do not document connection management or synchronisation operations." The cited guide describes its inventory coverage as all agents, not an unconfirmed subset.

claims.where: Governance controls: credential lifecycle; Governance guidance

claims.quote: When you need to rotate credentials, change the source scope, revoke access, or remove the connection, follow the relevant provider guide.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The connection page exposes synchronisation status and errors for administrators to review.
claims.quote:
Review the latest synchronization status.
Confirm the total number of synchronized agents.

claims.where: Governance guidance; Governance controls: missing-rows paragraph
claims.claim: The governance checklist directs readers to use controls that have no corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote:
Allow Agent 365's outbound IP addresses on the source platform if it restricts network access.
The checklist's source-platform IP allow-list, credential rotation and revocation, manual removal of registry agents, and synchronisation status review have no rows in the table.
claims.fix: The IP allow-list step before rollout and the manual-removal, credential-rotation/revocation and synchronisation-status steps after rollout have no corresponding rows. Remove those checklist directives while retaining the existing explanatory prose; acknowledging missing rows does not satisfy the checklist/table requirement.

claims.claim: Platform connection and registry synchronisation are administrative inventory operations rather than a change to how end users run source agents.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 connects supported platforms to a shared agent registry, giving administrators a cross-platform inventory while the agents continue to run where their teams built them.
